title: How Tipping Works at the End of a Kilimanjaro Climb
excerpt: Tipping the crew is a normal part of a Kilimanjaro climb. Here is how it usually works, who receives what and how to make sure tips reach the right people.
body:
At the end of a Kilimanjaro climb, climbers usually give a tip to the crew. For guides, cooks and porters, tips are an important part of their income. It helps to know how it works before you go.

## When and how

Tipping usually happens on the last evening or at the gate on the last day. Often there is a small ceremony with songs. Many climbers put the tip in envelopes per role, or hand the total to the group and announce the amounts so everyone knows what they receive.

## Who receives a tip

- Lead guide
- Assistant guides
- Cook
- Waiter or camp crew
- Porters

## How much

Amounts depend on route length, group size and crew size. Our partner shares suggested amounts per role per day when you book, so you can budget in advance. Tipping is always voluntary.

## Make sure it reaches everyone

Give tips directly to each crew member, or ask for an open distribution in front of the group. This avoids tips getting stuck with one person. Read more about [porter welfare](/blog/kilimanjaro-porter-welfare/).

## Cash

Bring US dollars in clean notes or Tanzanian shillings. See [money in Tanzania](/blog/tanzania-money-and-cards/).

## Gifts

Good-quality gear you no longer need (jackets, gloves, headlamps) is very welcome, in addition to a tip.

Read our general [tipping guide](/blog/tipping-tanzania/) or [plan your climb](/travel-proposal/).
